notes.title: Parallel conduction and Planckian scattering in FeTeSe
notes.summary: Connect optical parallel-channel fits with Planckian rate conventions and nonlinear resistance, while keeping the pairing mechanism unresolved.

review.scope: Selected author-version passages; final-version comparison and independent review pending.
limitations: Author self-review; no independent scientific review or raw-data reproduction.
Selected preprint passages, not a complete final published-version comparison.
The missing-area normalization and precise condensate fractions remain unresolved.

sections.title: What was measured
sections.markdown: Romero and colleagues analyzed complex terahertz conductivity alongside DC resistance in two FeTe1−xSex films. Their model separates a narrow Drude response from a much broader background. Within the measured frequency window, the narrow-channel width is approximately linear in temperature, while the total resistance need not be. The inferred condensate weight is mainly associated with that channel. This is an author-version interpretation, not a unique determination of the pairing interaction.

sections.title: Keep the frequency convention explicit
sections.markdown: For a Drude denominator $\Gamma-i\nu$, both variables use ordinary frequency. The corresponding pole decay rate is $\gamma=2\pi\Gamma$. Thus $\Gamma=\alpha k_BT/h$ and $\gamma=\alpha k_BT/\hbar$ express the same coefficient after conversion. The inherited reading note mixed these conventions. Its numerical expressions must not be copied unchanged.

sections.title: Why parallel channels matter
sections.markdown:
As a separate local illustration, take fixed $S>0$, $\sigma_0\geq0$, $c>0$, $\Gamma_0\geq0$ and $T>0$:

$$\sigma_{\rm DC}=\sigma_0+\frac{S}{\Gamma_0+cT},\qquad \rho_{\rm DC}=\frac{\Gamma_0+cT}{S+\sigma_0(\Gamma_0+cT)}.$$

Differentiation gives $d\rho_{\rm DC}/dT=cS/[S+\sigma_0(\Gamma_0+cT)]^2$. A linear narrow-channel rate therefore need not give linear total resistivity. When $\sigma_0=0$, this model does recover a linear resistivity. The approximation $\sigma_{\rm DC}=a+b/T$ additionally neglects $\Gamma_0$ and assumes sufficiently constant amplitudes. This algebra is not a fit to the experimental data.

sections.title: What remains unresolved
sections.markdown: The broad contribution is not resolved as an independent complete Drude peak. Its microscopic origin and a unique relaxation coefficient are therefore not established by this fit. The manuscript discusses nematic pairing qualitatively and leaves the mechanism open. Its printed missing-area prefactor requires comparison with the final paper and normalization before precise condensate fractions are imported. No third-party figures or full text are reproduced here.

notes.title: Nickelate strain: structural parallels, different mechanical paths
notes.summary: Compare measured lattice deformation, resistive criteria and orbital-model conclusions in strained La3Ni2O7 films without treating a structural correlation as a demonstrated pairing mechanism.

review.scope: Selected final published passages and figures, including transport, structural interpretation and methods. Supplement-wide and independent scientific review remain open.
limitations: Author self-review; no independent review or reproduction of imaging, transport or DFT data.
The full supplementary analysis, data repository and correction history have not been audited.
Structural association and hypothetical distortion calculations do not establish a unique pairing mechanism.

sections.title: Read the sample series before the headline
sections.markdown:
Bhatt and colleagues compare bilayer La3Ni2O7−δ films on four substrates. The final Figure 1 distinguishes nominal substrate mismatch from measured film strain. Negative values denote compression. The film on SLAO has a broad resistive transition; the other listed films do not establish superconductivity merely because one also has compressive strain.

| Substrate | Nominal strain | Measured strain | Reported transport in this study |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| SLAO | −2.0% | −1.6% | Onset near 42 K; zero resistance around 2 K |
| LAO | −1.2% | −0.9% | Metallic |
| NGO | +0.7% | +0.6% | Metallic |
| STO | +1.9% | +1.8% | Insulating |

These temperature endpoints belong to the SLAO film's ambient-pressure transport report, cited by the structural paper to Ko and colleagues. They are different criteria, not two interchangeable values of a precisely established bulk transition. The growth methods also differ: SLAO uses pulsed-laser deposition, whereas the main comparison films on LAO, NGO and STO use molecular-beam epitaxy. The authors do not definitively exclude sensitivity to synthesis details.

sections.title: Nominal mismatch is not the remaining film strain
sections.markdown:
The methods define nominal mismatch as $\epsilon_{\rm nom}=(a_{\rm sub}-a_{\rm bulk})/a_{\rm bulk}$, using the bulk pseudo-tetragonal reference $a_{\rm bulk}=3.833$ Å. The substrate values are 3.756, 3.787, 3.858 and 3.905 Å for SLAO, LAO, NGO and STO. Direct arithmetic reproduces the rounded nominal percentages in the table; it does not calculate the film's measured relaxation.

In-plane compression and higher octahedral symmetry are common features identified in the superconducting film and pressurized bulk structures. Their out-of-plane responses differ: the film can expand along the stacking direction while a hydrostatically compressed bulk sample contracts. This contrast does not convert epitaxial strain into an equivalent pressure. Nor does it establish that the SLAO film has the largest c-axis among all substrates.

sections.title: What the orbital calculations do and do not establish
sections.markdown:
The study decomposes structural changes into bond-length changes, internal-angle changes and rigid octahedral rotations. Calculations on those separated distortions are hypothetical controls, not independently prepared experimental samples. The reported suppression concerns local $t_{2g}$ admixture in predominantly $e_g$ low-energy bands; it is not a demonstration that the $d_{z^2}$ orbital disappears from the Fermi surface.

The final discussion says the importance of this reduced mixing for superconductivity remains to be established. Rotation effects are considered together with phenomenological Hubbard interactions. The calculations compare band structures, not a reproduced superconducting transition or a uniquely selected pairing mechanism. The metallic LAO film also has similar higher octahedral symmetry, so symmetry alone cannot be treated as a sufficient condition in this series.

sections.title: Keep local structure and superconductivity evidence distinct
sections.markdown:
STEM cannot directly identify which microscopic regions are superconducting. The paper examines defects, mixed structural phases and variable oxygen occupancy that can affect bulk-sensitive transport and diffraction. Its methods coordinate microscopy preparation and measurements within three days of oxygen annealing to mitigate oxygen loss. That protocol is part of the evidence context, not proof of exact oxygen stoichiometry.

The study reports 40 distinct ptychography fields of view for bond analysis. Thousands of bonds within those images are not thousands of independently synthesized superconducting specimens. A low-temperature reversal of oxygen-distortion direction, analogous to that reported in bulk, remains unresolved for the films. Raw imaging reconstructions, transport data, full supplements and DFT convergence have not been reproduced in this editorial check.

sections.title: Use the structural comparison as a constraint
sections.markdown: When comparing a new film, retain its growth and annealing history, composition, reference lattice, measured strain, local structural probe and transition criterion. Compare nominally similar samples before attributing transport changes solely to strain. This note connects the nickelate, strain and transport articles; it does not supply a validated recipe for raising the transition temperature.

notes.title: Eu-doped nickelates: re-entrance without a settled pairing mechanism
notes.summary: Separate sample-specific zero resistance, diamagnetic screening and resistance-contour criteria in Sm/Ca/Eu infinite-layer films; keep exchange compensation, magnetic order and pairing symmetry as distinct questions.

review.scope: Selected passages and figures in author manuscript arXiv:2508.14666v3 (25 April 2026), compared with the publisher abstract. The complete final published text has not been checked.
limitations: Author self-review, not independent scientific review or a reproduction of the transport measurements.
The later author version is not assumed identical to the final journal article; full final text, correction history, calibration and raw-data analysis remain open.
Resistance-contour criteria, zero resistance and screening are different observables. None alone settles the magnetic structure or pairing symmetry.

sections.title: Identify the material and the version
sections.markdown:
Yang and colleagues study Sm0.95−xCa0.05EuxNiO2 (SCEₓ), an infinite-layer nickelate film series with fixed nominal Ca substitution. It is not Eu-substituted bilayer La3Ni2O7. The measured Eu valence is mixed and varies with composition, so nominal x is not a direct count of identical Eu²⁺ moments.

This note reads the revised author manuscript dated 25 April 2026. The journal article was published online on 23 April 2026. The publisher abstract supports the broad re-entrance report, but access to that abstract does not establish equivalence of all final and author-version figures. The separate Nd/Eu nickelate study discussed in G3 and G5 concerns another material series; its magnetic interpretation cannot simply be transferred here.

sections.title: Keep each field scale with its sample and criterion
sections.markdown:
The selected author text and Figure 2 distinguish the following observations. Fields are perpendicular to the film plane (H∥c) for these comparisons.

| Sample | Temperature or protocol | Reported observation | Interpretation boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SCE0.34, about 54 unit cells | 2 K transport | Zero resistance returns above about 6.23 T | Recovery field, not a universal upper critical field |
| Same SCE0.34 specimen | Temperature sweeps at fixed field | Mutual-inductance screening at 9 and 12 T; absent at 3 T | Supports the superconducting interpretation; no bulk volume fraction is inferred here |
| SCE0.32 | 3 K transport | Resistance returns to zero near 13.04 T | Not the upper boundary of the high-field phase |
| SCE0.32 | 1.7 K transport | High-field zero resistance persists above about 32 T | Different temperature from the 13.04 T statement |

These temperatures describe measurement conditions, not interchangeable transition temperatures. Figure 3 instead marks open-circle phase boundaries using 0.5Rn, with Rn the high-field normal-state resistance. Those contours must not be relabeled zero-resistance boundaries. No material-Tc record is created from this table.

sections.title: Angular behavior and an unresolved inherited number
sections.markdown:
The angle θ is measured from the film normal. The angular maps use different temperatures: 4.2 K for x=0.33 and 0.36, 1.5 K for x=0.38, and 0.3 K for x=0.40. Their changing angular windows cannot support a universal assertion that in-plane re-entrance is absent. The manuscript also distinguishes intermediate-doping compensation-like behavior from stronger deviations at x=0.40.

The inherited notes attribute persistence to 45 T at 0.3 K to SCE0.36. That exact sample–temperature–field tuple was not verified in the selected v3 pages. Extended Data Figure 9 labels SCE0.36 at 4.2 K and SCE0.40 at 0.3 K; it also has a caption saying “up to 45 T” although its upper panels extend to 60 T. These version and panel details require resolution before the inherited tuple is used as a current verified result. A measurement ceiling would in any case provide a bound, not a measured high-field endpoint.

sections.title: What the magnetic evidence can and cannot establish
sections.markdown:
Nonlinear Hall response after linear-background subtraction and hysteretic magnetoresistance motivate magnetic explanations. They do not by themselves identify uniform ferromagnetism, its volume fraction, or a particular pairing state. The v3 discussion explicitly leaves long-range magnetic order and its structure undetermined.

The authors fit a WHH-based model including orbital and Pauli pair breaking, spin-orbit scattering and an exchange field. Compensation partially describes intermediate compositions; the fitted exchange fields and scattering parameters remain phenomenological. An empirical factor of two in a Brillouin-function argument improves some fits but is not universal and does not adequately describe x=0.40. Neither this adjustment nor analogy with other re-entrant systems proves spin-triplet pairing.

sections.title: Use the result across the Wiki
sections.markdown:
D5 supplies the material-family context; D15 separates substitution, scattering and magnetism; G3 and G5 distinguish re-entrance from a demonstrated compensation mechanism. For H7 and H9, superconducting recovery fields must not become Hall-sign-reversal or anomalous-Hall threshold fields. This note reports no extracted ordinary Hall coefficient.

A stronger scientific assessment still needs version-resolved final figures, criterion and noise-floor checks, sample calibration and local magnetic probes. The present review neither fits the deposited source-data files nor certifies an intrinsic bulk phase or unique microscopic mechanism.
